claim: On or about March 20, 2026, France's National Financial Prosecutor's office (the PNF) and the central office for combating corruption and financial crime searched the Paris offices of Edmond de Rothschild, the Swiss private bank, as part of a preliminary investigation arising from the released Epstein files. The probe centers on Fabrice Aidan, a former French diplomat who worked at the bank from 2014 to 2016 and whose name appears in more than 200 documents in the DOJ's Epstein production; investigators are examining suspected bribery of a foreign public official and complicity. The French investigative outlet Mediapart reported that the files suggest Aidan passed confidential United Nations material to Jeffrey Epstein. The bank said it was cooperating with investigators and had opened its own internal review. The search establishes that the Epstein documents have produced an active criminal investigation reaching a Rothschild-named institution; it does not, on its own, establish that any wrongdoing has been proven.
